- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and forecast is trending downward, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward adjustment.  
- If true outcome shows sharp spikes followed by sharp drops, model tends to over-forecast the spike — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next period.  
- If model consistently over-forecasts early in 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days), apply a 2–3% downward correction to early forecast points.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and true outcome deviates sharply from forecast, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average if deviation > 3σ.  
- For periods with high volatility (e.g., 2022-04-11 to 2022-04-21), reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±2% jitter around model to capture sudden shifts.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive spikes (e.g., 0.67, 1.00), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast growth rate by 15–20% after such events.
